Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Adequate funding needed for NCCE to fulfil its mandate – Agalga Source : Kareen Tei 23 November 2026 10:11am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Majority Leader and Chairman of Parliament's Committee on Independent Constitutional Bodies, James Agalga, has called for adequate funding for the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE), warning that the gap between its operational needs and available resources could affect its ability to carry out its constitutional responsibilities.
He has urged members of the Committee to advocate increased financial support for the Commission, particularly to enable it to effectively undertake its role in district-level elections and the ongoing constitutional review process.
Mr Agalga made the call when officials of the NCCE, led by its Chairperson, Kathleen Addy, appeared before the Committee to present the Commission's proposed 2027 budget estimates and review its performance in 2026.
The presentation covered the Commission's policy objectives, achievements and financial and non-financial performance under the theme, 'Upholding the Constitution in the Digital Age: Our Collective Responsibility'.
Mr Agalga expressed concern about the disparity between the Commission's operational requirements and its approved budget, stressing that adequate financial resources were essential for the NCCE to discharge its constitutional mandate effectively.
He called on Committee members to support efforts to secure the necessary funding to enable the Commission to carry out its activities and fulfil its responsibilities across the country.
Meanwhile, the Electoral Commission (EC), led by its Chairperson, Jean Mensa, also presented its 2026 performance report and outlined its proposed budget for 2027.
The Commission briefed the Committee on its staff capacity-building initiatives, the existing Constitutional Instrument (CI) and proposals for a new CI to govern the referendum, alongside its estimated financial requirements for next year.
Madam Mensa appealed for the timely approval and release of funds, explaining that 2027 would be a particularly busy year for the Commission.
She said early access to the funds would enable the EC to begin procurement processes and make adequate preparations for upcoming elections.
She stressed that the timely release of funds would allow the Commission to begin procurement and make the necessary preparations for the upcoming elections.
During the engagement, Committee members examined the Fund's performance and budget projections, seeking further explanations on key areas.
Following the deliberations, the Committee directed DACF officials to reappear on Thursday, November 26, to address outstanding issues and provide further clarification.
